name: PressedMail – Email Client, Inbox & Webmail
author: CurbSoftware Tech Innovations

sections.description:
Your email. Inside WordPress.

PressedMail is a full email client for WordPress that brings your existing inbox directly into the WordPress dashboard.

Read and organize messages, write replies, search your mailbox, manage folders and tags, and send WordPress website email, without constantly switching between WordPress and a separate webmail tab.

Connect your existing email address and keep using your current email provider. PressedMail works with standard IMAP and SMTP mailboxes, including many custom-domain and hosted email accounts.

PressedMail Free requires no PressedMail subscription, license key, or paid account.

A real inbox inside WordPress

PressedMail gives you a familiar email workspace directly inside the dashboard.

  • Read and manage your existing mailbox.
  • Compose new messages.
  • Reply, reply-all, and forward.
  • Use CC and BCC recipients.
  • Follow replies in threaded conversation view.
  • Use a signature for outgoing email.
  • Search and filter your messages.
  • Work from desktop, tablet, or phone.

Your email stays with your existing provider. PressedMail gives you a new way to work with it from WordPress.

Organize email your way

Keep customer messages, projects, orders, inquiries, and everyday email organized without leaving your website.

  • Browse and synchronize your provider’s email folders.
  • Create unlimited tags for your own workflow.
  • Search and filter messages within folders.
  • Move messages between folders.
  • Mark messages read or unread.
  • Delete unwanted email.
  • Quickly identify unread messages and attachments.

Whether WordPress is where you manage customers, content, orders, memberships, or client work, your inbox can now live beside the rest of your workflow.

A flexible email workspace

Configure PressedMail to suit the way you prefer to work.

  • Light and dark modes.
  • Responsive desktop, tablet, and mobile interface.
  • Adjustable inbox preferences and message-list behavior.
  • Basic keyboard navigation.
  • Optional dyslexia-friendly reading mode.
  • Configurable email behavior and reading preferences.

PressedMail is designed to feel like an email application rather than another WordPress settings screen.

Email with security controls built in

Email can contain untrusted content, tracking images, misleading senders, and potentially unsafe links. PressedMail includes controls designed to give you more visibility over what you open.

  • Messages are displayed in an isolated viewer to help contain untrusted content.
  • Remote images are blocked until you choose to display them.
  • Sender impersonation checks help identify potentially misleading identities.
  • Mailbox access follows WordPress permissions.
  • The connected mailbox is available to its owner.
  • Free receives plugin updates directly through WordPress.org.

These protections supplement, rather than replace, the security and filtering provided by your email provider.

Send WordPress email through SMTP

PressedMail can also handle email generated by WordPress itself.

Configure an outgoing mail server for messages such as:

  • Password reset emails.
  • New-user notifications.
  • Comment notifications.
  • WooCommerce emails that use WordPress mail.
  • Contact-form notifications that use WordPress mail.
  • Emails generated by plugins and themes through wp_mail().

You can send a test message before enabling the configuration.

PressedMail also includes a delivery log so administrators can check whether WordPress successfully attempted to send a message through the configured server.

You can:

  • Choose how long delivery-log entries are retained.
  • Clear the log manually.
  • Disable logging entirely.

The delivery log excludes message bodies and attachments.

WordPress notification sending is configured separately from your personal PressedMail inbox.

No PressedMail account required

PressedMail Free is designed to work independently.

There is:

  • No PressedMail subscription required.
  • No license key required.
  • No trial expiration.
  • No CurbSoftware telemetry.
  • No CurbSoftware analytics.
  • No custom update service.
  • No automatic connection to AI services.

Plugin updates are delivered through WordPress.org.

Your email provider’s normal service terms, storage limits, authentication requirements, and charges still apply.

Need more? PressedMail Pro expands the workspace

PressedMail Free is designed to be a useful standalone email client.

For users who manage multiple inboxes or want a larger email productivity workspace, PressedMail Pro adds additional capabilities.

Multiple accounts and one combined inbox

Connect multiple mailboxes and work across them from one unified inbox.

Contacts and calendar

Keep contacts and appointments beside your email instead of moving between separate applications.

Email automation

Create email rules and automatic actions for repetitive inbox tasks.

More control over timing

Use scheduled sending, snooze, and undo-send tools.

Optional AI tools

Use your configured AI provider for features such as writing assistance, summaries, tagging, and inbox organization.

Additional email-security tools

Run additional phishing and suspicious-message checks before acting on a message.

More ways to personalize PressedMail

Use additional themes, layouts, signatures, and signature rules to create the workspace you prefer.

PressedMail Pro is a separate GPL-compatible paid plugin and is not included in the WordPress.org download.

AI features use the provider you configure. Provider usage charges may apply.

Explore PressedMail Pro or compare Free and Pro features.

Who is PressedMail for?

PressedMail can be particularly useful when WordPress is already the center of your work.

For example:

  • Website owners who want their business inbox beside their site.
  • WooCommerce store owners handling customer conversations.
  • Freelancers and agencies managing client communication.
  • Membership and community administrators.
  • Content teams working primarily inside WordPress.
  • Small businesses using custom-domain email.
  • Administrators who want both an inbox and WordPress SMTP tools in one plugin.

Instead of opening WordPress, webmail, contacts, and other tools separately, PressedMail brings more of that workflow into one place.

Help and documentation

Need help connecting your mailbox?

PressedMail setup documentation

For help with the WordPress.org version:

WordPress.org support forum

Privacy and External Services

PressedMail Free has no CurbSoftware telemetry, analytics, license checks, or custom update checks. Free receives updates only through WordPress.org.

Installing or activating PressedMail does not send email content or mailbox metadata to CurbSoftware or an AI service.

External connections occur only when required by a configured email service or when initiated by an authorized user.

Your IMAP server

PressedMail connects to the IMAP host and port you configure in order to work with your mailbox.

Depending on the requested action, this may include:

  • Listing folders.
  • Synchronizing messages.
  • Searching email.
  • Reading messages.
  • Moving messages.
  • Changing flags.
  • Deleting messages.

Using the security settings you configure, PressedMail sends the mailbox username or email address, credential or OAuth access token, and the mailbox commands required for the requested action.

Your mail provider may return information including folders, message identifiers, senders, recipients, dates, subjects, headers, message bodies, attachments, flags, labels, and synchronization state.

Your email provider’s terms of service and privacy policy apply to that connection.

Your SMTP server

PressedMail connects to the SMTP host and port you configure when you send email from PressedMail or when WordPress sends website notifications through the configured mail server.

Using your configured security settings, the SMTP connection may transmit:

  • Authentication information.
  • Sender information.
  • Recipients.
  • Subject.
  • Headers.
  • Message body.
  • Attachments.

Your email provider’s terms of service and privacy policy apply to that connection.

Optional Microsoft sign-in

Microsoft sign-in uses Microsoft’s identity services together with the PressedMail Microsoft OAuth relay.

Password and app-password connections do not use this relay.

When Microsoft sign-in is started:

https://pressedmail.com/oauth/microsoft/start

receives the site URL, WordPress administrator callback URL, and a cryptographic nonce.

After Microsoft redirects the authorized user back:

https://pressedmail.com/oauth/microsoft/redeem

receives the one-time transfer code, site URL, and the same nonce.

When a replacement access token is required:

https://pressedmail.com/oauth/microsoft/refresh

receives the refresh token, site URL, and a fresh nonce.

The relay returns mailbox identity information, access and refresh tokens, granted scope, and token-expiry information to your WordPress site.

The relay does not receive message bodies, attachments, or mailbox contents.

Microsoft receives the authentication and authorization information required by Microsoft’s identity and mail services.

PressedMail Terms of Service

PressedMail Privacy Policy

Microsoft Services Agreement

Microsoft Privacy Statement

Remote images

Remote images in email are blocked by default.

If you choose to display a remote image, your browser requests that image directly from its host.

The remote host may receive information such as:

  • The requested image URL.
  • Your IP address.
  • Your browser user agent.
  • Browser headers.
  • Cookies associated with that host, where applicable.

The remote host’s own terms and privacy policy apply.

Because senders can use remotely hosted images for tracking, displaying an image may reveal that a message was viewed.

Local storage and sending logs

Account settings, encrypted credentials or OAuth tokens, and synchronized mailbox information are stored in your WordPress database or filesystem as required by PressedMail.

The site owner controls the site’s:

  • Hosting.
  • Database.
  • Filesystem.
  • Access.
  • Backups.
  • Data retention.
  • Account removal.
  • Personal-data requests.
  • Uninstall cleanup.

The optional WordPress notification delivery log records:

  • Date.
  • First recipient.
  • Recipient count.
  • Subject.
  • Sender.
  • Mail server.
  • Sending result.

Message bodies, headers, and attachments are not stored in this log.

Entries expire according to the retention period you select. Logging can also be disabled or cleared manually.

Development

Source code and build instructions

Human-readable source code and build instructions for the PressedMail Free interface are publicly available.

  • Source repository
  • Source for version 1.0.26
  • Build instructions for version 1.0.26

The repository includes the readable TypeScript, React, CSS, manifests, lockfile, and build configuration used to create the Free interface assets under assets/admin/dist/.

PressedMail Pro source code is not included in the WordPress.org package or the Free source distribution.

To build the Plate.js/Vite interface from the repository root, use Node.js 20+ and pnpm 11:

pnpm install && pnpm build

Open-source libraries and assets

PressedMail Free uses WordPress’s registered React, ReactDOM, and JSX runtime.

Libraries include:

  • Plate.js: MIT
  • Slate: MIT
  • Vite: MIT
  • Tailwind CSS: MIT
  • Radix UI: MIT
  • KaTeX: MIT
  • date-fns: MIT
  • Zod: MIT
  • React Aria: Apache-2.0
  • DOMPurify: Apache-2.0 or MPL-2.0

OpenDyslexic is distributed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. OFL.txt is included beside the bundled font files.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New and search for PressedMail.
  2. Install and activate the plugin.
  3. Open PressedMail from the admin sidebar.
  4. Connect your mailbox using its provider settings or supported sign-in method.
  5. Open your inbox and start reading and replying.

For website notifications, configure WordPress email sending in Settings and send a test message.
sections.faq:
What do I need to use PressedMail?

A WordPress site you control and a compatible IMAP/SMTP account. Your provider continues to host your mailbox; your web host must allow connections to it.

Which email providers can I connect?

Compatible providers include many custom-domain and cPanel mailboxes, Gmail, Google Workspace, Outlook, Microsoft 365, Zoho Mail, and Fastmail.

Gmail uses app passwords where permitted; Microsoft accounts can use Microsoft sign-in where supported. Availability depends on provider, plan, and organization settings. Additional configuration may be required.

Can I use the free plugin without a paid account?

Yes. Free requires no PressedMail account or payment and never expires. Your email provider’s terms and charges still apply.

How does website email sending work?

Messages generated through WordPress’s standard wp_mail() system can use your configured SMTP server. Inbox messages use the connected mailbox’s sending settings.

The log reports sending results, not guaranteed placement in the recipient’s inbox.

Can I move to Pro later?

Yes. Pro is designed to preserve compatible accounts, settings, and local data when it replaces Free. Follow the installation guidance supplied with Pro.
sections.changelog:
1.0.26

  • The Explore PressedMail Pro buttons on the About page are readable again in every theme. WordPress admin’s own link colour was overriding the button label; links the plugin renders as buttons now keep their theme colours.

1.0.25

  • The plugin’s REST routes now live under one prefixed namespace, pressedmail/v1. The unprefixed api/v1 mirror is gone, so PressedMail can no longer collide with another plugin that uses that name.

1.0.24

  • Maintenance release. Nothing changes in the free edition; the version is kept in step with the paid edition, which had a fix.

1.0.23

  • Tables in an email are readable again instead of being squeezed into columns about a character wide.
  • Opening a message is faster on modest hosting: the bodies for the page you are looking at load ahead of the click, and that work pauses whenever a mailbox sync is running.
  • The background-sync notice has a Reload button, and the expired-session notice now reloads the page, which is what it always told you to do.

1.0.22

  • Tag and signature capabilities no longer report a maximum or a remaining count. Nothing was limited, so there is nothing to count; the plugin simply says what you can do.
  • Calendar invitations are sent from the organiser’s own mailbox instead of the site’s mail server, so they are no longer relayed by a server that is not authorised for the sender’s domain.
  • WordPress email settings ask one clear question about which mailer sends site email, and say plainly that your PressedMail inboxes are unaffected either way.

1.0.21

  • A snooze whose message cannot be parked now stops after three tries, stays in the Snoozed list as “Snooze failed, still in “, and posts a notification, instead of retrying forever in the background.
  • A tab left open past the sign-in nonce lifetime recovers its session on the next request instead of asking for a reload.
  • Background delivery of scheduled sends, snooze returns and undo-send no longer runs inside inbox reads; it runs from the sync driver and WordPress cron, where it has room.

1.0.20

  • Sweep can create a rule for any destination: a named folder, Archive, Junk or Trash, in one account or a Combined Inbox. Before, anything but Junk or Trash answered “A destination folder is required.” even though the sweep itself ran.
  • Dialog and popover headings keep their own size and colour instead of inheriting WordPress admin heading styles.

1.0.19

  • Search now reads contact list membership through a shared helper that every build contains, instead of one that only some builds do.

1.0.18

  • Calendar reminders no longer stop a background tick on a site that changed packages while keeping its calendar data.

1.0.17

  • The public source repository now contains only the code the free build compiles. It is generated from the same policy that governs the shipped bundle, so the two cannot drift apart again.
  • Every compiled translation now ships with the readable .po it was compiled from.
  • Removed unreachable code: two parked sync features, an unused model, a duplicate readme, and the development-only asset loader.
  • Plan and licensing wording that could never be displayed is no longer compiled into this build.

1.0.16

  • The Free package now contains only direct remote-image loading. The separately distributed image proxy implementation is physically absent.

1.0.15

  • The header search input now matches the selected PressedMail theme instead of using the white WordPress admin background.
  • Vite asset errors no longer include local filesystem paths.
  • The mailbox lock sanitizes its plugin-owned browser grant cookie before validating it.

1.0.14

  • Free now contains only its complete, working feature set. Source for the separately distributed paid plugin is physically absent.
  • Remote images load directly after the user chooses to display them. The separate image proxy implementation is no longer included.
  • Mailbox, signature, system-email server, provider, and keyboard-shortcut behavior now use direct Free implementations.
  • The readme links directly to the public source repository and build instructions.
  • Internal transient names now use the full PressedMail prefix.
